mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕“诗歌”话题，涵盖读诗入门（Reading）、李白与诗仙风骨（Extended reading）和人生的选择（Integrated skills：未选择的路）三个子话题——诗歌鉴赏与人生感悟是高考读写结合的常见落点，也是雅思文学教育类议论文的命题区。

subTopics.title: 读诗入门
subTopics.desc: 课文方法论：即使真意 beyond your grasp，也可以先听 how the poem sounds——set the poem aside and come back to it later。

prompts.task: 你班英语角将举办“诗歌之夜”活动，不少同学因“读不懂诗”而犹豫。请你写一篇短文发在班级群里，分享读诗的方法，鼓励大家参加，内容包括：1. 理解同学的顾虑；2. 两三条读诗建议；3. 邀请参加。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Poetry Night Is for Everyone

Many of you told me, "I'd love to come, but poems are beyond my grasp." Please don't worry — nobody understands every poem, not even poets themselves!

Here are my tips. First, read the poem aloud: even if its true meaning escapes you, you can always enjoy how it sounds. Second, don't chase the "correct answer"; more than any other type of literature, poetry implies meanings beyond the words on the page, and your feeling is a valid key. Third, if you still don't get it, simply set the poem aside and come back to it later — good poems wait patiently.

This Friday, bring your favourite lines and your curiosity. See you at Poetry Night!

prompts.task: Some people think that poetry is no longer relevant in the modern world. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
In a culture of instant messages and shrinking attention, poetry can look like a museum piece: beautiful, respected and read by almost no one. I disagree with the claim that it has lost relevance — though I concede that poetry's presence has changed shape, and that its traditional packaging has indeed dated.

The case for irrelevance is easily made. Poetry sales are a rounding error in publishing; school encounters with verse are often the last; and the modern reader, trained by feeds to skim, has little patience for lines that must be read twice. If relevance means market share, the argument is over quickly.

But relevance measured by use tells another story. Whenever language must carry more feeling than information, people reach instinctively for the poetic: at weddings and funerals, in anthems and protest slogans, in the careful words of a love message. Song lyrics — poetry's loudest descendant — are memorised by billions who would never open a verse collection, and short poems now travel social media precisely because compression is the native art of the small screen. More deeply, poetry answers a need the information age sharpens rather than solves: it slows the reader down, saying less and meaning more, in a world that says more and means less. A form built on implying what cannot quite be said will stay relevant for as long as humans feel more than they can state.

My conclusion is that poetry has not retreated from modern life; it has dissolved into it. The book of verse sells poorly — while its contents, wearing new clothes, are everywhere.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):表态精确('disagree + concede 包装过时'),反方以'市场份额'立论并被'使用度'框架反转,支持段三层(仪式语言/歌词与社媒短诗/信息时代的减速需求),结论'没有退场、只是溶解'收束——程度与机制兼备。

Coherence & Cohesion(连贯与衔接):'The case for irrelevance is easily made'/'But relevance measured by use tells another story'/'My conclusion is...'——衡量标准的切换即论证枢纽;'saying less and meaning more / says more and means less'的镜像对句是全文之眼;'wearing new clothes'收尾呼应'traditional packaging has dated'。

Lexical Resource(词汇资源):'a museum piece'、'a rounding error in publishing'、'trained by feeds to skim'、'poetry's loudest descendant'、'compression is the native art of the small screen'、'dissolved into it'——原创密集;课文命题(imply meaning beyond words)转写为'implying what cannot quite be said'。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法准确性):冒号定义、分号并列论据、whenever 从句、for as long as 从句、破折号反转收尾;复杂句准确。
vsGaokao: 体裁:高考是班级群动员帖(顾虑+方法+邀请);雅思论诗歌的时代价值——教人读诗vs为诗辩护。
论据来源:本文用歌词/社媒/仪式语言的社会观察;动员帖用课文读诗三法(读出声/别追标准答案/先放一放)。
语域:群帖有'good poems wait patiently'的温柔;雅思以'wearing new clothes, everywhere'的机智收束。
评分维度:雅思看'相关性如何衡量'的框架创新;高考看方法实用、语气亲和、动员有效。

subTopics.title: 诗仙李白
subTopics.desc: 课文评传：dare not speak in a voice loud 的惊人想象——free expression of strong feelings breathes vitality into his poetry。

prompts.task: 你的英国笔友 Oliver 正在学中文诗歌，来信请你介绍一位中国诗人。请你写一封回信介绍李白，内容包括：1. 诗人简介；2. 他的诗风特点（可举诗句）；3. 推荐一首入门作品。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Oliver,

How wonderful that you're learning Chinese poetry! Let me introduce Li Bai, the poet every Chinese child can recite.

Living in the Tang Dynasty, Li Bai travelled famous mountains and great rivers all his life, encountering different customs and writing over a thousand poems. What makes him special is his striking imagination and free expression of strong feelings, which breathes vitality into everything he describes. In one early poem, standing in a mountain temple at night, he wrote: "I dare not speak in a voice loud, for fear of scaring dwellers on high" — as if the stars were just above his head!

For a start, try Quiet Night Thoughts, four simple lines about moonlight and homesickness. Short as it is, it has comforted Chinese hearts for 1,200 years.

Yours,
Li Hua
vocabHints: travel famous mountains and great rivers
dare not speak in a voice loud

prompts.task: Some people believe that schools should spend more time teaching the classical literature of their own country, while others think this time would be better spent on modern practical skills. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
How many classroom hours a nation owes its old poets is a genuine dilemma for modern curricula. Practical-minded reformers would trade classical literature for coding and communication; traditionalists call that trade a quiet self-erasure. My own view is that classical literature is itself a practical subject, wrongly accused — though it must be taught as a living thing, not a museum duty.

The reformers' case is sincere. Employers do not interview candidates on ancient verse; hours are scarce, and a syllabus is a budget. If education's first duty is to equip the young for work, then spreadsheets, statistics and second languages have obvious claims, and the centuries-old poem looks like an heirloom lovingly kept while the house needs repairs.

Yet the opposition mistakes what classical literature actually trains. A student who works through an old poem is decoding compressed language, weighing ambiguity and reconstructing a distant mind — precisely the interpretive muscles that contracts, negotiations and cross-cultural work demand. Classics are also a nation's shared memory: they supply the images and phrases through which citizens recognise one another, and a generation cut off from them becomes a guest in its own culture. Nor is the past impractical: a poet who turned exile into imperishable lines teaches resilience more memorably than any workshop.

My conclusion is that the choice is misdrawn. Teach the classics, but teach them as their authors wrote them — as living speech about love, loss and mountains — and they will quietly deliver the very skills the reformers demand: close reading, deep memory and a self that knows where it stands.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):双观点公允(改革派:课时预算与就业问责;传统派:解读肌肉+共享记忆+韧性教育),立场'古典文学本身就是实用学科'反转对立框架,结论给出教学方式条件('as living speech')——讨论落到怎么教。

Coherence & Cohesion(连贯与衔接):'The reformers' case is sincere'/'Yet the opposition mistakes what classical literature actually trains'/'My conclusion is that the choice is misdrawn'——推进有力;'an heirloom lovingly kept while the house needs repairs'与'a guest in its own culture'两个比喻分别锚定两段;'living speech'收尾呼应'living thing'。

Lexical Resource(词汇资源):'a quiet self-erasure'、'a syllabus is a budget'、'interpretive muscles'、'a nation's shared memory'、'turned exile into imperishable lines'(李白匿名化用)、'a self that knows where it stands'——概念警句密集。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法准确性):条件从句('If education's first duty is...')、破折号插入定义、nor 倒装('Nor is the past impractical')、祈使式结论;句式多样准确。
vsGaokao: 素材用法:李白在回信中点名介绍并引诗句英译;雅思中化为'a poet who turned exile into imperishable lines'——诗人的两种出场方式。

subTopics.title: 为诗歌发声
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：advocate reading poetry、meet one's ideals、live up to an ideal——在快节奏的时代，仍有人愿意为诗歌的理想发声。

prompts.task: 有同学认为读诗'没用'。请你以校诗社名义用英文写一篇短文，为读诗辩护，内容包括：1. 回应质疑；2. 说明读诗的价值；3. 发出邀请。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
"Why read poetry? It's useless." We in the Poetry Society hear this a lot, and today we'd like to answer it.

We strongly advocate reading poetry, not because it helps you pass exams, but because it does something exams cannot. A good poem teaches you to notice — a falling leaf, a quiet grief, a sudden joy — and to say what you feel in a way that lives up to the feeling itself. Poetry keeps alive an old ideal: that language can be beautiful as well as useful.

So we invite you to give it a real chance. Come to our reading evening this Friday, choose one poem, and read it aloud. You may be surprised how much a few lines can hold. See you there!
vocabHints: lives up to the feeling itself

prompts.task: Some people believe that the ability to write well, for example keeping a diary or composing poems, is a valuable skill that everyone should develop. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
In an age of voice messages and video, the ability to write well can seem old-fashioned. Yet I strongly agree that everyone should develop it, because writing does far more than transmit information — it clarifies thought, preserves experience and gives feeling a lasting shape.

The most practical benefit is mental. Putting ideas into sentences forces us to organise them; we often discover that we do not truly understand something until we try to write it down. Keeping a diary, for instance, turns a confused day into something we can examine and learn from, and personal writing of this kind is widely found to reduce stress and sharpen self-awareness. Creative forms such as poetry go further, training us to observe closely and to choose words with care — skills that improve all communication, not only art.

Writing also serves memory and connection. A recorded conversation vanishes, but a letter or journal can be reread for decades, preserving thoughts and emotions that would otherwise be lost. In work and study, moreover, the person who can write a clear report or a persuasive argument holds a lasting advantage over one who cannot.

It is true that not everyone will write poems or novels, and that spoken skills matter too. But the basic ability to express oneself clearly and thoughtfully on paper is within almost everyone's reach and rewards the effort for a lifetime.

In conclusion, I firmly believe that writing well is a skill worth developing for all. Far from a relic of the past, it remains one of the surest ways to think clearly, remember deeply and be truly understood.

subTopics.title: 人生的选择：未选择的路
subTopics.desc: 课件诗篇：弗罗斯特笔下 two roads 的抉择——to where it bent in the undergrowth，人生岔路口的思考。

prompts.task: 你校英文报以 "My Road Not Taken" 为主题征文，请你结合弗罗斯特的诗《未选择的路》（The Road Not Taken），写一篇短文讲述你的一次选择经历，内容包括：1. 你面对的选择；2. 你的决定及原因；3. 你的感悟。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
My Road Not Taken

Last year, two roads lay before me: joining the school orchestra, where most of my friends went, or the tiny poetry club that nobody chose.

Like the traveller in Frost's poem, I stood long at the fork, looking down one path to where it bent in the undergrowth. Finally I took the one less travelled by — the poetry club — because something in me wanted a quieter road.

One year on, I have hosted our first Poetry Night and found my own voice on paper. I still wonder, sometimes, about the road not taken; but I have learned that what matters is not choosing the perfect road, but walking your chosen one with all your heart — and that has made all the difference.
vocabHints: to where it bent in the undergrowth

prompts.task: Some people think young people should follow the paths their parents suggest, while others believe young people should make their own choices about their lives. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
At every fork in a young life — subjects, careers, cities, partners — two voices offer directions: the parents' and the person's own. Some travellers trust the older map; others insist the road must be chosen by the feet that will walk it. My position is that parents deserve a hearing and the young deserve the decision, because advice ages better than obedience.

The case for parental guidance is built on real assets. Parents hold decades of data the young cannot yet possess: they have watched talents rise and markets fall, and their warnings often encode painful experience compressed into a sentence. Their motives are also uniquely reliable — few advisers on earth want our flourishing so undividedly. Where the young see romance in a road, parents see its winters, and both visions are true.

Yet the decision itself belongs, by right and by logic, to the one who must live it. A path chosen by others is walked without ownership: when hardship comes — and every road bends into undergrowth eventually — the obedient traveller asks 'why did they send me here?', while the self-chosen traveller asks 'how do I go on?'. Only the second question builds an adult. Moreover, parents' maps, however loving, chart the world they knew; roads change faster than advice, and yesterday's safe route may be today's dead end.

My conclusion is a division of labour: let parents light the crossroads, and let the young do the choosing. A wrong road walked with whole-hearted ownership teaches more than a right road walked on borrowed conviction — and it is the walker, at last, who must answer for the miles.
